transcript:
Header: 2026-10-07 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~62 mins | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samir Khan (Redwood AE); Jules Park (Redwood SE); Leah Martinez (NovaMarket CTO); Tom O'Neill (Head of Partnerships); Ravi Patel (Platform Eng)
---
Summary: quick sync on marketplace listing and technical integration; align on reference arch and pilot steps
Topics: listing metadata, private connector, VPC, SSO, KMS, billing mapping, timeline
---
00:00 Samir Khan: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i'm samir from redwood, i'll kick off. can you hear me okay?
00:05 Leah Martinez: yep loud and clear, thanks samir.
00:10 Samir Khan: great. quick intro round real quick please?
00:15 Tom O'Neill: tom o'neill, partnerships at novamarket, hi all.
00:20 Jules Park: jules park, solutions engineering, i'll cover the arch and the integration bits.
00:25 Ravi Patel: ravi here, platform eng, i'll own the vpc and network work on our side.
00:30 Samir Khan: perfect, today's goal is to align on the marketplace listing requirements and the technical flow for a joint solution — hosted redwood listing plus optional private connector for sensitive customers.
00:42 Leah Martinez: great, we're keen to get the listing up Q4 and have a reference arch we can point customers to. procurement's asking for SSO and KMS details early.
00:52 Jules Park: sure, i'll show a draft arch in a sec. quick question, what's your desired billing model for the listing — revenue share, referral fee, or co-managed pricing?
01:00 Tom O'Neill: we were thinking revenue share initially, but need the mapping for usage attribution. can redwood emit per-account usage tags?
01:08 Samir Khan: yes, we can attach tenant ids to usage and provide per-tenant breakdowns in the console; we'll also provide an S3 export and billing CSV for reconciliation. note: there may be a short delay in full attribution during batched processing.
01:20 Ravi Patel: okay good. on the private connector side we need how redwood expects to authenticate into our VPC and which ports.
01:28 Jules Park: expected flow is a customer-managed VPC peering or private link; we also support egress-only connectors where redwood calls out over an outbound vpn. for the initial pilot we recommend a simple private endpoint with mutual TLS.
01:40 Ravi Patel: ok and IP allowlist? we have strict egress rules, may need NATing on our side.
01:46 Samir Khan: we can provide a small set of egress IPs but for scale dedicated pools have dynamic ranges, so mutual TLS or a private link is more stable. i'll note that we must avoid putting static global ip dependence.
01:58 Tom O'Neill: re: security, procurement asked for SOC2, audit logs, and SSO. do you have an enterprise pack for marketplace partners?
02:06 Samir Khan: yes we have SOC2 reports, can share redacted copies; for SSO we support SAML and OIDC for console access, and RBAC can be mapped to your partner roles.
02:16 Leah Martinez: KMS — can we keep keys in our KMS and have redwood encrypt in transit only? or do you need keys for envelope encryption?
02:24 Jules Park: the typical pattern is customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption keys; redwood supports external KMS integrations (KMS or HSM). for some hosted features we do envelope keys but customer keys can be used for long-term storage. slightly messy wording from our side there.
02:40 Ravi Patel: also data residency: some customers require EU-region-only storage, can we pin region per-tenant?
02:46 Samir Khan: yes we have region pinning options for dedicated and private deployments; hosted listing can indicate available regions and we can route EU tenants to EU-backed infra. there's some nuance on cold backups, we'll document it.
03:00 Tom O'Neill: great. can you run us through the reference arch?
03:05 Jules Park: sure i'm sharing my screen — calling out the components: marketplace listing -> redirect to partner doc -> hosted API (redwood) for standard customers -> private connector for sensitive customers -> VPC peering or outbound VPN -> tenant KV cache sits on the redwood side but kv was typed as K-V cash in one of our older notes so ignore that misspelling, sorry.
03:30 Leah Martinez: ha, ok. for the private connector flow can you show auth sequence?
03:35 Jules Park: 1) customer provisions test VPC and allows redwood via private link or mTLS; 2) they create service account for redwood with limited IAM; 3) redwood uses that to fetch model artifacts and maintain KV cache for request prefixes. note: transcription may say K-V cash earlier — that's the system cache.
03:58 Ravi Patel: do you support SAML attribute mapping so we can pass partner account ids?
04:03 Samir Khan: yes, we accept SAML mappings; we can also accept SCIM for provisioning if that's helpful.
04:10 Tom O'Neill: any constraints on sequence length or model variants for the marketplace listing? some customers will want long context models.
04:18 Jules Park: we document max sequence lengths per model in the catalog; for long context workloads we recommend specific variants and can suggest quantization profiles to reduce cost. for the listing we'll include a recommended performance profile per workload.
04:34 Leah Martinez: how realistic is it to include an 'on-premable' option (air-gapped) for regulated customers?
04:40 Samir Khan: we do a private deployment offering that can run on-prem with an air-gapped install, but that's enterprise and requires separate licensing. we can signal that in the listing as "Private / On-prem available, contact sales".
04:55 Ravi Patel: ok makes sense. on telemetry — what do you expect us to forward for joint observability?
05:02 Jules Park: we typically add request id headers and emit metrics; we can integrate with your prometheus/grafana endpoints via pushgateway or syslog for audit logs. we also provide token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
05:18 Tom O'Neill: will the marketplace listing support trial credits or free-tier usage?
05:23 Samir Khan: yes, we can configure promo credits and free-tier offers on the listing page. procurement might want to bundle trials for top customers.
05:30 Leah Martinez: earlier you said attribution could be delayed due to batching — how big a delay are we talking?
05:36 Samir Khan: typically a few minutes, rarely more than 30 minutes; but for bulk ingest in high-throughput we might do hourly rollups. we'll document SLAs around that.
05:48 Ravi Patel: network requirements — i'll need exact ports, cidrs, and cert formats to configure our side. can you put that in a checklist?
05:55 Samir Khan: yes, i'll send a network checklist and the marketplace asset list (logos, 512px, descriptions, pricing fields).
06:02 Jules Park: i'll produce the initial reference architecture diagram and a short runbook for the private connector steps.
06:08 Leah Martinez: perfect. on timelines, procurement wants to go fast — can we aim to have a pilot by mid-nov?
06:15 Samir Khan: that's doable — proposed timeline: 2 weeks to share artifacts, 1 week for NovaMarket to provision test VPC, 2 weeks for SE-led integration and smoke tests, then pilot start. that's about 5-6 weeks which fits mid-nov target.
06:30 Tom O'Neill: any blockers we should pre-surface? legal needs to see data processing addendum and support for vendor questionnaires.
06:36 Samir Khan: we'll attach our DPA and security packet; legal review often takes time so start that parallel to tech work.
06:44 Leah Martinez: ok action items and owners?
06:48 Samir Khan: i'll summarize in email but main owners are samir for listing assets, jules for arch/runbook, ravi for test vpc, leah to coordinate procurement.
06:58 Tom O'Neill: cool, one more question — what's the expected engineering involvement from redwood during pilot? say 2-3 engineers or less?
07:06 Jules Park: initial pilot usually needs 1 SE + 1 backend engineer for the heavier parts; we can scale up if we encounter network nuances.
07:15 Ravi Patel: sounds good. i'll try to have dev resources assigned once we have checklist.
07:20 Samir Khan: perfect. we'll also share a checklist doc and a short spreadsheet for billing mapping.
07:27 Leah Martinez: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
07:30 Samir Khan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the assets and schedule the demo for the week of 10/19.
07:36 Tom O'Neill: thanks, bye.
07:38 Jules Park: bye.
---
Artifacts referenced: marketplace_asset_checklist.xlsx (Samir to share link), reference_arch_draft.png (Jules to drop in shared drive), security_packet_redwood.pdf (Samir), billing_mapping_template.csv (Samir)
